title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 27-29): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, purely combinatorial 'analysis situs'. Its ingredients are as follows.
- A set L of 'points' and a family of 'pieces' X, Y, Z, ordered by <= (presumably 'is a face/sub-piece of').
- An incidence relation x << X, meaning x lies in the closure of X. It is also used between pieces: Z << X means Z lies in the closure of X.
- A 'strict' incidence relation, written <<° here for the circled double-less-than in the image. x <<° X means X is minimal among the X'' <= X with x << X''. Geometrically, x lies in the open part (relative interior) of X.
- omb(X) ('ombre', the shadow) = {x in L : x << X}, the closed cell. omb(X)° = {x : x <<° X}, the open cell.
- ML1, ML2, ML3 are axioms. ML2 guarantees omb(Z)° is non-empty. ML1 'renforcé' gives existence of intermediate pieces.

Inputs from p. 27:
- Lemma 2: if x <<° Z and x << X', then Z << X'; moreover x <<° X' iff Z <<° X'.
- Hence, for Z << X there is X' <= X with Z <<° X'.
- Lemma 1 (used on p. 29): omb(X')° meeting omb(X'') forces X' <= X''.

This page:
- Cor. 1: for Z << X there is X' <= X with Z <<° X'. So every piece in the closure of X lies 'openly' in some sub-piece of X.
- Cor. 2: for Z << X and X' <= X, the following are equivalent:
  - (i) Z << X';
  - (ibis) omb(Z) ⊂ omb(X');
  - (ii) omb(Z)° ⊂ omb(X');
  - (iii) omb(Z)° ∩ omb(X') ≠ ∅.
  The non-trivial step (iii) ⇒ (i) is exactly Lemma 2: pick x <<° Z with x << X'. This is a 'condition of the frontier': if the open stratum of Z meets the closure of X', then the whole of Z lies in the closure of X'.
- Cor. 3: the following are equivalent:
  - (i) Z <<° X';
  - (ii) omb(Z)° ⊂ omb(X')°;
  - (iii) omb(Z)° ∩ omb(X')° ≠ ∅;
  - (iv) X' is minimal in X̃^Z = {X' in X̃ : Z << X'};
  - (v) X' is the smallest element of X̃^Z.
  Proofs given:
  - (i) ⇒ (ii): take any x in omb(Z)° (non-empty by ML2) and apply Lemma 2.
  - (iii) ⇒ (v): continued on p. 29, take x in both open cells and apply Lemma 1.
  - The remaining implications are trivial.
- Consequence (p. 29, mislabelled again 'Cor. 3'): transitivity of the strict relation, i.e. X <<° Y <<° Z ⇒ X <<° Z.

Purpose: show that the axioms force the pieces to behave like the closed strata of a stratification (or cells of a regular cell complex). The open strata partition the points, closure inclusion is detected by a single point, and each piece has a unique smallest 'carrier'. This prepares the introduction of a separation relation || on L (axiom ML0) on the next page.
errors: Corollary 3, (i) ⇒ (ii): the written argument ends with 'donc (iii)' (or is so transcribed). The argument actually works for every x in omb(Z)°, so it yields (ii) directly. This is a minor labelling slip, not a mathematical gap.

Corollary 2 relies on Lemma 2, which in turn rests on axioms ML1 (in its 'generalised/reinforced' form), which p. 27 says are 'admitted'. Correctness is relative to these axioms, which are not stated on this page.
Numbering: on p. 29 the transitivity statement is again called 'Corollaire 3'. It should be Corollary 4.
The implication diagram '(v) ⇓ (i) ⇔ (iv)' is loosely written. (v) ⇒ (iv) is trivial, but (i) ⇔ (iv) is essentially the definition of <<° only after Cor. 1 / Lemma 2, so it is not quite 'trivial'.

ideas.what: Points/pieces incidence axiomatics with closed shadow omb(X) and open shadow omb(X)°. Each point lies in the open part of a unique minimal piece.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification / regular cell-complex face poset; carrier (support) of a point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratifications); combinatorial cell-complex theory (Björner et al.)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (1984). The detailed axiomatics stays in unpublished 'Analysis situs' manuscripts.

ideas.what: Cor. 2: the open stratum of Z meets the closure of X' iff Z lies in the closure of X'.
ideas.modern_name: Condition of the frontier (frontier condition) for stratifications

ideas.what: Cor. 3: open cells intersect iff contained iff X' is the least element containing Z; transitivity of strict incidence.
ideas.modern_name: Partition into open strata; unique minimal carrier; strict incidence as a partial order

missed.claim: This page is part of an unpublished axiomatic derivation of the frontier condition and of the partition into open strata from point/piece incidence axioms (ML1-ML3). It is an attempt at a synthetic 'tame topology' foundation. The page-level content is routine stratification combinatorics. The overall axiom system, which is unpublished, may be of documentary interest for o-minimality and tame-topology historiography.
missed.quote: Il suffit de voir (iii) ⇒ (i), et c'est ce qu'on a vu dans le lemme précédent.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck tried to axiomatise tame topology combinatorially (shadows/'ombres'), rather than via o-minimal structures. That is relevant to histories of the Esquisse tame-topology programme, but it carries no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are routine consequences of the axioms (frontier condition, unique carrier, transitivity) for stratified/cellular structures. The only interest is archival: they belong to Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' of 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'comb(Z)', 'comb(X')' should read 'omb(Z)', 'omb(X')' (ombre = shadow), consistent with p. 29.
In Corollary 1, 'Z <<° X' ⊆ X' is better read as 'Z <<° X' ≦ X' (the order relation on pieces).
In Corollary 2, the vertical sign under X is '≤' (X' ≤ X), i.e. X' ranges over pieces below X.
The crossed-out heading line reads 'Corollaire 4' (or 'Corollaire'), followed by 'Soit' and crossed-out 'Conditions équivalentes'.
In Corollary 3, (i) ⇒ (ii) ends '... i.e. x ∈ omb(X')°, donc (ii)'. The last line reads 'Prouvons que X' est plus petit dans X̃^Z, i.e.'
